guia.what: A contextual message block within the content, not full width. It’s the place for clarifications, warnings, and tips that sit right next to what they explain. It supports a title, actions, and a close button.
whenUse: The clarification only makes sense next to what it accompanies (a step, a field, a paragraph).
You want to highlight something in the content without taking the user away from where they are.
You need hierarchy by variant (info, success, warning, danger) within the page.
whenAvoid: The status applies to the whole page or app → `banner`.
It’s ephemeral and doesn’t need to stay written down → `toast`.
It’s only a short status label, with no prose → `badge`.
dos: Place the note next to what it explains, not at the end of the page.
Use `ts note-title` when the body runs longer than one line. It gives the gist at a glance.
donts: Don’t sprinkle notes every other paragraph. If everything is highlighted, nothing is.
Don’t put essential information in a dismissible note.

nucleo: The dismissible note hides with its close button, and Core handles that. The `data-ts-dismiss` button hides the note (`data-ts-dismissible`) and notifies with `ts:change`. Without a close button it is static markup.
